source.title: Open Problem: Tight Bounds for Kernelized Multi-Armed Bandits with Bernoulli Rewards

accepted.question_text: In a kernelized Bernoulli bandit, a learner sequentially chooses actions x_t from a decision set X contained in R^d and observes Bernoulli rewards y_t sampled with mean f(x_t), where the unknown function f: X -> [0,1] belongs to the reproducing kernel Hilbert space H_k induced by a kernel k, has known RKHS norm bound ||f||_{H_k} <= B, and satisfies k(x,x) <= 1 for every x in X. Given the history G_t = {(x_s, y_s)}_{s=1}^{t-1} of past action-reward pairs, can one construct an effective estimator of f(x) at a new point x in X that uses the kernel structure while producing estimates appropriate for Bernoulli mean parameters in [0,1]?

accepted.question_text: In a kernelized Bernoulli bandit with unknown f: X -> [0,1] in an RKHS H_k, ||f||_{H_k} <= B, k(x,x) <= 1, and observations y_t sampled from Ber(f(x_t)), can one define a suitable estimator mu_t(x) of f(x) and prove concentration guarantees for the deviation |f(x) - mu_t(x)| that are tight for Bernoulli observations rather than merely using the fact that Bernoulli rewards are 1/2-subgaussian? More specifically, can such guarantees capture the stronger Bernoulli KL-divergence concentration rates known for unstructured multi-armed bandits while handling the correlations among arms induced by the kernelized setting?

accepted.question_text: For a finite-action kernelized Bernoulli bandit under the RKHS regularity conditions f in H_k, ||f||_{H_k} <= B, and k(x,x) <= 1, can one design regret-minimization algorithms whose regret grows logarithmically in the horizon T and whose instance-dependent dependence is governed by the Bernoulli KL divergence d(f(x), f(x*)) between each action's mean and the optimal mean f(x*)? Can such a logarithmic, KL-dependent guarantee be achieved in the kernelized setting where the kernel may encode correlations among arms, noting that the trivial kernel k(x,x') = 1{x = x'} reduces the finite kernelized bandit to an unstructured multi-armed bandit?
